sections.h2: What does the Sheboygan County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Sheboygan County Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages and other land documents for every parcel in the county, and it also keeps vital records and files plats and Certified Survey Maps. Its own page describes the land records it holds as representing $11 billion in real estate.

The office does more than file paper. Its listed duties include:

  • Recording deeds, mortgages and liens, including federal tax liens.
  • Accepting new subdivision plats and Certified Survey Maps.
  • Registering births, marriages and deaths.
  • Handling the informal probate step called Termination of Decedent's Interest.
  • Collecting the state transfer fee and reporting it to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue.

The office says recorded land records are the basis of the real estate property tax, and it reports transfer fee collections and property values to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue. The county's treasurer and real property staff, its planning office and its highway department also depend on the office for information.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Sheboygan County?
sections.html:
The recording fee for most documents is $30, set by state law and the same in every Wisconsin county. When the seller transfers a house, a state transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value is added.

ItemAmountSource
Recording most documents$30Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag)
Termination of Decedent's Interest$30 regardless of pagesSheboygan County Register of Deeds
Copy of a recorded document$2 for the first page, $1 for each added pageWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(b)2
Certifying a copy$1 extraWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(b)2
Real estate transfer fee30 cents per $100 of valueWis. Stat. 77.22(1)

The transfer fee works out to $3 per $1,000. On a sale at $232,700, the Census median owner-occupied home value for Sheboygan County, the fee would be about $698. The office also posts a Fee Schedule page for its other charges, so check it before you send a check.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Sheboygan County?
sections.html:
You can record by mail or in person, or a title company or lender can record electronically. Under Wis. Stat. 706.05, an instrument offered for record must carry the signatures the law requires and identify the land and the parties well enough to be indexed. A document that affects a particular parcel must include the full legal description, and every conveyance of an interest in real property must come with the transfer return.

The return is filed online with the Department of Revenue. Under Wis. Stat. 77.22, a completed return and the register's collection of the fee are prerequisites to accepting the deed for recording. The register has no duty to check the value you report or the exemption you claim, so enter both with care.

Sheboygan County accepts e-recording through listed vendors: CSC sRecording Solutions, ePN, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. The county says electronic recording began on August 5, 2008, that it accepted its first e-recorded deed on January 20, 2010, and that the system normally records, indexes and returns the image in about 24 hours. For paper documents, the office page also mentions SWIFT, a service that returns paper documents by email under an agreement with the county.

sections.h2: Which Sheboygan County transfers pay no transfer fee?
sections.html:
Several kinds of transfer are exempt from the state fee, and the deed must state the reason by citing the exemption. Wis. Stat. 77.25 lists them. Common ones for homeowners include:

  • A transfer by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A foreclosure deed, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, to a mortgage holder or a land contract seller.
  • A transfer between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration.
  • A transfer between an individual and a domestic partner.
  • A deed that corrects or confirms an earlier recorded conveyance for nominal or no consideration.
  • A conveyance of real estate worth $1,000 or less.

Even when no fee is due, the transfer return is still part of the filing. Sheboygan County's pages for Termination of Decedent's Interest and for Transfer by Affidavit ($50,000 and under) both say an electronic return is required. The affidavit is recorded in the register's office only if real estate is involved.

sections.h2: What should a Sheboygan County seller know about the county?
sections.html:
Sheboygan County sits on Lake Michigan between Manitowoc County to the north and Ozaukee County to the south. It covers 1,271 square miles, of which 511 are land, and its cities are Sheboygan, Plymouth and Sheboygan Falls. Sheboygan is the county seat and the largest. The Census Bureau estimated the county at 118,047 people on July 1, 2025.

The Census QuickFacts numbers for 2020-2024 give a picture of the housing market:

  • The median value of an owner-occupied home is $232,700, and 71.5% of housing units are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent is $934, and median household income is $73,094.
  • The county issued 364 building permits in 2025, and the average trip to work is 18.2 minutes.

The shoreline matters to a seller too. The Wisconsin Shipwreck Coast National Marine Sanctuary, created in 2021, lies in Lake Michigan waters off the county. If your parcel is on the lakefront or a river, ask the Register of Deeds for copies of any recorded easements or surveys before you list.

sections.h2: How can a Sheboygan County owner guard against deed fraud?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds offers a free Property Fraud Alert that monitors land records filed in the county; you sign up at propertyfraudalert.com. It emails you when a document is recorded against your name or parcel, which gives you time to act.

The alert reports a filing after it is recorded, so it works as an early warning. State law says the register has no duty to check the value or an exemption claimed on a transfer return (Wis. Stat. 77.22(1)), which means the owner is the one best placed to notice something wrong. If a filing looks false, call the Register of Deeds and ask what the document is, then talk to a real estate attorney and your title insurer.

sections.h2: What should a Sheboygan County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Before closing, collect the recorded deed that put you on title, confirm the legal description matches the deed you plan to sign, and ask the title company who will record and by what method. If the house passed to you through a joint tenancy or a life estate, a Termination of Decedent's Interest may need to be recorded first. The county asks for a copy of the document that shows the joint tenancy, life estate, survivorship marital property, vendor's interest or mortgagee's interest, along with the $30 fee and the electronic return.

If you have questions about a specific document, contact the Register of Deeds directly; the office has forms for foreclosures and Sheriff deed guidelines on its Real Estate page.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Sheboygan County?
faqs.a: It costs $30 for most documents. Wisconsin sets the recording fee by statute, so it is the same in every county, and Sheboygan County lists the same $30 for a Termination of Decedent's Interest regardless of page count.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate transfer fee in Sheboygan County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. Wis. Stat. 77.22(1) puts the fee, 30 cents for each $100 of value, on the grantor, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted for recording.
Yes. The county lists CSC sRecording Solutions, ePN, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile as vendors, and it says e-recorded documents are normally recorded and returned in about 24 hours.

faqs.q: Do I need a transfer return when I inherit a house in Sheboygan County?
faqs.a: Yes, an electronic return is still required. A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is exempt from the fee under Wis. Stat. 77.25, but the county's Termination of Decedent's Interest page says the return must be filed online with the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Can Sheboygan County alert me if someone records a document against my property?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register of Deeds offers a free Property Fraud Alert through propertyfraudalert.com. It monitors activity involving land records filed in the county and notifies you when something is recorded.
